usual_baseline: Pre-incision timing usually good: 100% within 60 minutes [1497], over 95% within two hours [1198]. Choice and duration are the problems. Correct agent 65.4% [1497]; duration compliant 64.4% [1497]; postprocedural appropriateness 48.3% [1373]. Full compliance with three post-op doses 54.2% [1527]. Overall compliance 58–64% [1373, 1376].
fix_that_works: A new agreed protocol with pamphlet and theatre poster cut spinal prophylaxis from up to two weeks to 24 hours in all patients [1389]. Posters in anaesthetic rooms raised correct induction antibiotic choice from 18% to 94% [1321].
fix_that_fails: Stickers on nursing care bundles: MRSA eradication therapy prescribed 1% to 8% [1321].
consultant_advice: Most of these audits never closed the loop. Timing is rarely the problem, so don't audit it alone. Measure choice and post-op duration and overuse, especially in joint replacement, where compliance was 40% [1497], and re-audit.
